NovaBiotech Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBiotech Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. [Standard operator instructions for Q&A participation.]

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBiotech Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Mark Reilly, Chief Executive Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Reilly, CEO of NovaBiotech Therapeutics.

Mark Reilly, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBiotech Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust demand across our oncology and rare disease franchises, continued market share gains in key immuno-oncology indications, and early momentum in our GLP-1 portfolio. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including pipeline advancement, manufacturing scale-up, and commercial execution in a competitive landscape.

Today, I'll provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives. We achieved another quarter of double-digit revenue growth, fueled by NeoVira, our PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific antibody, which exceeded expectations in metastatic NSCLC, alongside solid contributions from our gene therapy assets and emerging GLP-1 offerings. Our diversified portfolio across oncology, rare diseases, immunology, and metabolic disorders positions us well for sustained growth. We're particularly excited about NeoVira and its potential to capture meaningful share in the $200 billion-plus immuno-oncology market, supported by positive Phase III data and upcoming label expansions.

We've also advanced key technical initiatives, such as AI-driven drug discovery platforms that are accelerating our hit-to-lead timelines, and we're navigating biosimilar pressures while investing heavily in next-generation modalities like ADCs and degraders. With that foundation, I'll now turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO:
Thank you, Mark, and good morning, everyone. As Mark highlighted, we had a solid third quarter. Total net product revenues reached $2.85 billion, an increase of 18% compared to the same period last year and 5% sequentially. This marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit growth, outpacing the broader pharma market. Excluding a $150 million one-time milestone from our Pfizer partnership on the Zynova CAR-T program, underlying growth was 14% year-over-year. Oncology drove the lion's share at $1.48 billion, up 22%, led by NeoVira's $1.12 billion in sales—beating our guidance midpoint by $50 million—as U.S. total Rx share hit 28% in metastatic NSCLC per Symphony Health data, chipping away at incumbents like Keytruda ahead of its 2028 patent expiry.

Rare diseases and gene therapies added $850 million, up 12%, with GeneForge, our AAV therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, delivering $620 million on replenishment demand following label expansion into presymptomatic infants, now holding 65% U.S. market share. Immunology came in at $520 million, flat year-over-year due to biosimilar impacts on our TNF legacy asset but buoyed by ramps from InflamX, our oral JAK-STAT degrader in Phase III for ulcerative colitis.

Regionally, the U.S. at 72% of revenues grew 20% to $2.05 billion, thanks to formulary wins and orphan pricing stability despite IRA headwinds. Europe added $515 million, up 11% at constant currency, with NeoVira's EMA adjuvant approval unlocking $80 million in demand, though Germany's AMNOG reforms trimmed a couple points. Emerging markets surged 25% to $285 million, powered by China tenders via our WuXi JV.

Our GAAP gross margin expanded to 82.4%, up 410 basis points sequentially and 320 basis points year-over-year. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding one-time inventory adjustments from our small-molecule divestiture, it reached 83.1%—our 10th consecutive quarter of expansion. Product mix added about 150 basis points, as NeoVira ramped to $450 million quarterly—up 45% year-over-year—with mid-80s margins from its premium IO positioning, offsetting biosimilars like our adalimumab at 65-70%. Volumes on biosimilars grew 120% year-over-year, capturing post-Humira scale.

Pricing dynamics contributed 100 basis points: modest 2-3% ASP hikes on NeoVira in the U.S. (55% of revenues) amid KOL demand and PBM favor, 1% net erosion in Europe from HTA pressures mitigated by label expansions, and 5% uplift in Asia-Pacific on NeoVera via Sinopharm amid the booming GLP-1 market.

Manufacturing efficiencies were the star, delivering over 200 basis points—exceeding guidance—with COGS per unit for biologics down 18% year-over-year to $42 per gram. At our Limerick, Ireland greenfield site, a 22% yield boost in mammalian cell culture for NeoVira came from perfusive chromatography and PAT sensors, shortening batch cycles to 90 days. Continuous manufacturing pilots for NeoVera at Lonza Singapore cut purification costs 15%. U.S. sites in Boston and San Diego saw 12% savings via single-use bioreactors; Ireland leveraged tax incentives but dual-sourced APIs amid India disruptions; Singapore hit 8 g/L titers at 25% lower costs.

We're committing $500 million over two years to Industry 4.0, including AI predictive maintenance and digital twins, already trimming 8% off variables, targeting 30% COGS cuts for CAR-T. We'll insource 60% high-margin fill-finish by 2026 while outsourcing biosimilars to partners like Dr. Reddy's for resilience. Q4 margins guide to 83-84%, FY24 at 81.5-82%, offsetting raw material inflation like 15% HEPES hikes and IRA risks.

GAAP net income was $500 million, or $1.50 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $800 million, or $2.85 per share, beating consensus by $0.22. Operating expenses were $1.42 billion, up 9%, with R&D at 28% of revenues—disciplined versus peers. Adjusted EBITDA hit $1.05 billion, or 37% margin. Cash stands strong at $4.2 billion, funding $3.5-4 billion FY24 CapEx, including our $1.2 billion Boston cell/gene hub. We repurchased $300 million in shares.

Turning to marketing and sales effectiveness, our metrics show robust execution per IQVIA and ScriptTrx, benchmarked to Lilly and Merck. Sales force productivity rose 12% quarter-over-quarter via omnichannel and AI HCP targeting, sustaining double-digit NRx growth.

For NeoVera, our GLP-1 for obesity and diabetes, Q3 net sales were $1.2 billion, up 28%, with 4.2 million TRx at 22% U.S. obesity share—gaining on Mounjaro/Wegovy. NRx hit 1.1 million, up 35%, from 150,000 detailing calls averaging 18 per rep weekly, with 24% reach uplift among endocrinologists/PCPs. ROPS improved to 4.2x via 15% budget shift to digital closed-loop, yielding 42% higher script lift. U.S. dominated at 85%, Europe NRx up 52% QoQ to 450,000 on tenders and 95% formulary placement; emerging markets like Brazil/India added 8% sales with 65% NRx growth.

Oncology's ONCO-456, akin to NeoVira's PD-1 profile for NSCLC/melanoma, posted $850 million, up 19%, with 14% first-line NSCLC share, 2.8 million TRx, and 28% NRx acceleration. Our 220 specialized reps delivered 95,000 email details and 120,000 virtual iPad interactions—60/40 field/digital mix boosting efficiency 31%. Share of voice hit 26% via ESMO/ASCO KOLs showing 15% OS benefit; ROPS at 3.6x, digital portal converting 18% to scripts.

GeneForge rare disease sales surged 40% to $180 million post-label expansion, with 50 reps at 28 calls weekly covering 92% top treaters, 45% conversion, and 75% 12-month adherence via HUB program for 5.2x ROPS.

Tech-wise, Salesforce Einstein segments 250,000 providers, lifting top-line 22%; Veeva CRM closes 68% digital to scripts. NeoVera's app has 1.2 million downloads, 55% engagement cutting discontinuations 14%. Amid 340B/IRA, promotional spend guides 18-20% of sales, 25% digital/evidence; Q4 brings ONCO-456 companion diagnostics with Roche and compliant DTC for NeoVera.

On pricing and reimbursement, U.S. (62% of NovaCure/NeoVira revenues at $1.2 billion) saw GTN at 38%, up 200 bps from PBM rebates (52% per script) and 340B. Net realization 68% of $142,000 WAC, via preferred status on 85% lives. IRA models 3-5% erosion, offset by PAPs covering 28,000 patients; GeneForge exempt as orphan biologic, with RWE for NCD. DIR mitigated via GPOs at ASP+6%; outcomes rebates with UnitedHealthcare.

Europe/ex-US (28%, $540 million): full EU5 reimbursement at €98,000 post-clawbacks; NICE/HAS ICER £42,000/QALY; Germany 22% discount countered by risk-sharing. China NRDL at RMB 680,000 won 90% VBP share, up 35% sales. Biosimilars pressure TNF 15%, but lifecycle defenses hold.

Strategies include value-based pricing on 40% contracts, $150 million RWE with Flatiron/TriNetX for 15% Spain uplift, next-gen bispecific BLA H1 2025, Global Access in 50 countries. GTN guides 37-39%, coverage 95%; mid-single ASP growth 2025.

For the full year, we're raising guidance to revenue of $11.4-11.6 billion, up from $11.2-11.5 billion, and adjusted EPS to $10.90-11.10 from $10.70-10.90, baking in NeoVira upside and China ramps.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Mark.

Mark Reilly, CEO:
Thank you, Elena. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator instructions.] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Elena, on gross margins, that 200 basis point beat from manufacturing was impressive—can you talk more about the sustainability into FY25, especially with raw material inflation and potential IRA clawbacks? And how does the $500 million Industry 4.0 spend factor in?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO:
Thanks, John. Absolutely, sustainability is baked into our flywheel. The efficiencies from Limerick's yield improvements and Singapore's perfusion modes are now at scale, with Q4 guiding 83-84%. Raw materials like HEPES up 15% are more than offset by the 18% COGS drop and digital twins reducing downtime 8%. Industry 4.0's AI predictive maintenance targets 30% further cuts for CAR-T, and insourcing high-margin work balances CMO shifts. IRA risks are modeled, but our 84-86% FY25 target holds firm, funding the $3 billion R&D pipeline with three Phase III readouts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen, Morgan Stanley:
Great, thanks. On the sales metrics, the NRx acceleration on NeoVera and oncology looks strong—how are you thinking about Q4 promotional spend allocation, especially with digital ROI outpacing field, and any updates on biosimilar defenses?

Mark Reilly, CEO:
Thanks, Lisa. Dr. Patel and I are thrilled with the omnichannel shift—ROPS at 4.2x for NeoVera and 3.6x in oncology reflect that 60/40 mix and Einstein AI boosting conversions 22%. Q4 spend stays 18-20% of sales, with 25% more to digital and evidence gen, including DTC pilots and Roche companion diagnostics. Biosimilar defenses are robust—NeoVira's patent thicket to 2032 and lifecycle next-gen filing H1 2025 stave off challengers, as seen in our 3-point share gain.

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer:
To add, Lisa, our ESMO/ASCO data on OS benefits and RWE from ADHERE/ Hubs are key to KOL loyalty and adherence, supporting refill loyalty.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez, JPMorgan:
Thanks. Elena, pricing held up well despite GTN creep—thoughts on IRA Part D impact for Medicare-exposed assets and Europe HTA trends? Also, emerging markets outlook?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO:
Good question, Mike. U.S. GTN at 38% is managed via 92% reimbursement parity and outcomes rebates tying to PFS. IRA caps model 3-5% ASP hit for 15% Medicare on NeoVira, offset by PAP expansions. Europe HTAs like NICE are favorable at low ICERs, Germany's risk-sharing caps refunds; China VBP wins 90% share. Emerging like Brazil/India grow 12% CAGR with local offsets—guiding flat-to-down 2% U.S. net pricing FY24, mid-single growth 2025.

Operator:
[No further questions at this time.]

Mark Reilly, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We're confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities—from NeoVira catalysts and four H1 2025 PDUFAs to AI-biotech M&A—and deliver long-term value for our shareholders amid sector consolidation.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBiotech Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
